Status: now = available now, wip = in progress, plan = planned (a decision stands behind it, no date), open = an open question. Every 'now' must point at something that exists today.

use.title: Use Silent Zero
use.description: What you can look at today and what is still to come, for the people who will run Silent Zero.
use.lede: Silent Zero is a small operating system for machines where AI acts in the physical world. You cannot install it yet. This page says what you can look at today and what is still to come.
items: AI agents that deliver work and, increasingly, move arms or wheels. Silent Zero treats every agent as untrusted, whatever model drives it, and keeps the agent's authority and the machine's safety beneath it.
A graphical loader checks the seL4 kernel image, shows the result and starts the kernel. 24 seconds of video.
The proven part of the kernel does what its specification says. Everything else is labelled tested or assumed and never passed off as proven; firmware and graphics hardware stay trusted.

By design, processor time is held like memory: an agent cannot starve the control loop, and a small deterministic loop has the last word on every motion. Timing bounds for modern processors are not yet proven.
The code is BSD-2-Clause, the paper and the texts CC BY 4.0.
Discussions for questions and ideas, Issues for a flaw or a wrong claim.
A bootable image, first in an emulator.
Checksums and signatures, and how to verify them before you boot.
A first board, then a list of what runs on what.

Not yet. Today's commercial robot stacks list certificates (PikeOS) or work towards them (NVIDIA Halos); the seL4 Foundation's own page names none. How a proof becomes evidence for a certification body is open, and we promise no route to a certificate.

devel.title: Develop with Silent Zero
devel.description: For people who build, verify or want to look inside Silent Zero: where to start, what works, how to take part.
devel.lede: For people who build, verify or just want to look inside. Everything here is open; the label says what works today.

involved.heading: Get involved
involved.text: We are looking for people who know firmware, formal verification or robots, and who want to test this argument before the architecture hardens around it.

items: What the parts are and why nothing at the base is new.
What is proven, what is assumed
The kernel page lists the proof status per configuration: proven, not stated, tested, assumed.
The loader (under 8 KB on RISC-V), the splash renderer and the build scripts.
Needs clang with the RISC-V target, ld.lld and QEMU; make test boots a good image and tampered ones. The steps are in the README; not yet checked on a clean machine.
Where we are unsure and want help
Every wiki page ends with its open questions; the Issues collect what the team has to decide.
A model proposes, the proof checker judges. The wiki collects what is known.
